Chapter 13

The sequencer

One writer, a cached high-water mark, and a check that catches the botched deploy where two engines are running.

By the end of this chapter

Build the only thing allowed to assign sequence numbers, and the check that proves it is alone.

The sequencer is the venue's total order made concrete. It is the one place a command is given its position in history.

Proving nobody else is writing

Why on every batch rather than at startup

The failure appears mid-life, not at boot. Both processes start correctly — the second one reads the high-water mark and gets a sensible answer. It is only once both are appending that they diverge, and by then a startup check is long past.

Validating on the way in

The gateway already validated the command. The sequencer validates it again, and the duplication is deliberate.

Bug found: a drill script poisoned the log

That validation was added because of a real incident, and the chain of consequences is worth following.

A test script fired the kill switch directly at the sequencer, bypassing the gateway. It sent firmId where the command schema wanted targetFirmId. TypeScript did not catch it, because the script used a cast — and a cast is a promise the compiler has no way to check.

  1. The malformed command was written to the append-only log, permanently.
  2. The engine applied it and produced a kill_switch_changed event whose firmId was undefined.
  3. The projector enqueued an outbox message from that event, with no firm.
  4. The worker tried to send the email, passed undefined to a database parameter, and failed.
  5. It retried. Six times. Reporting "undefined cannot be passed as argument to the database" — an error about the database, describing a problem three layers upstream and an hour earlier.

That is what a poisoned log looks like from the outside: a confusing error, in the wrong component, long after the cause. The fix is the parse above — and a second fix in the worker, so that a malformed payload dead-letters immediately with a clear message instead of retrying eight times to prove what the first attempt established.

Checkpoint

  • You can explain why the sequencer caches its high-water mark
  • You can explain why assertSoleWriter runs on every batch
  • You can explain why validating twice is worth it at the boundary of an append-only log
